target_customer: Military forces and defense buyers seeking low-cost precision strike
problem: Precision strike is rationed because each round is expensive, so forces see more targets than they can afford to hit.
business_model: Hardware sales of missiles and launchers to defense customers (stated intent, no contracts found)
product_category: Defense hardware, guided short-range ballistic missiles and launchers

founders.name: Henrijs
prior_employers: Two defense companies building autonomous systems fielded by NATO forces (names not given on the YC page)
education: Astra Nova (formerly Ad Astra), first international cohort, aerospace and mechanical engineering focus
founders.background_notes: Only a first name appears on the YC page. Other team members are described only by employer, for example NASA JPL, Caltech GALCIT, US Army DEVCOM ARL and Imperial College London.

competitors.name: Castelion
competitors.what: Builds low-cost mass-produced hypersonic missiles (Blackbeard) for the US Army
competitors.traction_then: Reported by Fortune in October 2026 and other outlets as a major Army program; a search summary cites a $1B raise at a $13B valuation, not independently verified here

competitors.name: Ares Industries
competitors.what: YC-backed maker of low-cost cruise missiles
competitors.traction_then: Covered by Fortune in 2024 as YC's first weapons bet
competitors.funding_then: Pre-seed from CoastCap and Y Combinator per a directory

technical_complexity.rationale: Guided ballistic missiles need propulsion, guidance, in-house propellant production and launcher integration with drone targeting, all by a team of three in a regulated domain.

defensibility.rationale: Export controls, security clearances and production know-how are hard to replicate, but well-funded rivals already hold Army relationships and the company has no demonstrated product yet.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well-resourced low-cost missile makers and a US Army low-cost strike program were already active at founding. No takeover or copying outcome is known yet.

market_need_then: US and allied forces are pursuing cheaper strike munitions; the Army has an Affordable High Speed Strike effort and a Low-Cost Containerized Missiles program per 2026 coverage (search results, TWZ and DTR).

branding.domain_note: Uses polemosindustries.com with the Industries suffix. An unrelated gaming and crypto firm named Polemos exists.

identity.visual_style: Muted industrial imagery of launchers in misty or desert landscapes
identity.voice_and_tone: Terse, declarative, mission-driven, for example 'Precision strike, engineered for production'

brand_strength.rationale: Site copy is crisp but the name is unexplained and collides with another Polemos, and no press about the brand exists yet.

outcome_analysis: Polemos joined YC in Fall 2026 with a three-person team and no public funding, customers or press. Its idea sits in a hot defense niche with funded rivals such as Castelion, so its path depends on a working prototype and government access. It is too early to call; no shutdown or acquisition was found.
notes: Funding search returned only a different Polemos (a gaming firm with a $14M seed), which is excluded. Founder surname not found. Competitor Castelion figures come from a search summary and one outlet; treat as unverified. Greek meaning of Polemos as war is general knowledge, not a company statement.
